The memory module's rules, given once in this session, each with its reason:
Record each memory at the RE whose goal it serves, never at a PE that provides for it. Why: The Join rule attaches all knowledge to the RE, so the next agent finds a memory where the goal it serves is borne, and memory cannot tell an RE from a PE for you.

How to use memory_read_unread, given once in this session:
node: The map element whose memories the command acts on, element:<address>. Without node, receiver, provider or address the command acts on the whole memory graph.
receiver: A purpose whose memories the command acts on: the address of the element that holds it, with provider.
provider: A purpose whose memories the command acts on: the address of the element that serves it, with receiver.
address: An element, by address; with receiver and provider, the element at that address the join holds.

To work a ticket handed to you: read it with id=; op=plan with the steps you plan; op=step as each finishes, saying what you did and any choice you made with its why; op=done with a resolution and a why when it is complete; when you stop with it open, op=edit its note to say what is true now and where. op: list, the default; add; edit, which, when you stop with your ticket open, sets its note to what is true now and where; take, which says an agent has started on the task; plan, which says how many steps you plan, first, and again when the plan changes; step, which says you finished one, with what you did and any choice you made and why; move, which puts it in a column of the board; distribute, which gives the open tickets the glyphs of N agents; glyphs, which reads the available agent glyph names; or done, which closes it with its resolution and why once the work is complete.

A work record is attached to one element or join and never changes the map. Its condition is the state of that part, never the kind of ticket: most tasks carry none. A stage, unbuilt, under-construction or built, says where the part is on its way to existing; built marks nothing. broken is a built part that does not do its job. The intake and the person set it, since they judge the state of the part; an agent at work says what it found in its own ticket's note instead. Its note says what and where, its task what it needs. How to use map_work, given once in this session:
node: list, add and edit: an element, by address; edit moves the ticket there, keeping its progress. list gives its own records and those on the joins it receives or provides.
receiver: list, add and edit: a join, by the address of the element that holds it, with provider.
provider: list, add and edit: a join, by the address of an element it holds, with receiver.
condition: add, edit, and list as a filter: the state of the part the record is at, never the kind of ticket. missing is intended functionality that is absent, a finding. A stage, unbuilt, under-construction or built, says where the part is on its way to existing; built is the normal state and marks nothing. broken is a built part that does not do its job. A task on a part that exists and works carries none. The intake and the person set it, since they judge the state of the part; an agent at work says what it found in its note instead. condition=none on edit clears it.
kind: add, edit, and list as a filter: what sort of work the ticket is, never the state of the part: broken, a fix for a part that does not do its job; flawed, a part that works but is not right; enhancement, a part that works and could be better; or none for a plain task. kind=none on edit clears it.
links: add and edit: other nodes the task links for reference, a list of element addresses, and of objects of receiver and provider, with address for a part inside, each naming a purpose.
held: add and edit: put it in Backlog, where it waits: no agent starter starts it, Autostart, Start all, Distribute and an agent's glyph among them; the person releases it to To do or starts it on its own. A ticket an agent of Metaform writes is always held, and releasing one is the person's decision.
agent: add and edit: the agent this ticket prefers, claude, codex or gemini; the person can change it at any time, even while an agent works on it.
hold: add and edit: true holds the ticket, hidden from agents and automatic starts until the person lets it go; list: true lists held tickets too.
glyph: edit: the agent glyph the ticket is assigned to; tickets with the same glyph are one agent's, done one at a time.
eligible: add and edit: the eligible agent types as a JSON list, claude, codex or gemini; [] allows Any agent, the default for existing and new tickets. Dispatch and agent claims honor it.
after_work: add and edit: the work ids this ticket waits on, as a JSON list; no agent starts it automatically until each of them is done. [] waits on none.
title: add, required, and edit: one short line saying what the ticket is. The ticket takes the next number at its node, shown as <address>#<n>.
